scenes.title: The Ninth Key
scenes.summary: Saturday morning at the front desk: F1, M1, and M2 open the dusty cedar box stamped 'Room 9' with the small brass key.
scenes.intro: It is early Saturday morning at {SHOW} in {CITY}, just hours after {M1} carried a dusty cedar box stamped 'Room 9' up from the cellar. {F1} and {M2} lean over the front desk as {M1} turns the tiny brass key. Listen to the scene first.
story: Turn the small key slowly, {M1}—my heart is beating fast!
Relax, boss. A brass lock from the cellar never breaks.
It clicked! Lift the wooden lid, {M1}!
Inside we have... one big door key, a blue plan, and postcards.
Read the top of that folded blue paper! Where are my glasses?
Still on your forehead, {M2}, right where you left them last night.
Aha! Look here: 'Ground Floor — Room Nine — Garden Sunroom'!
Wait, we have a garden sunroom on the ground floor?!
Look at the arrow behind the back hallway bookcase.
That heavy wooden bookcase has stood against that wall for twenty years!
Then behind those old books, there is a ninth door!
Drink one sip of coffee first—then we move the books.
scenes.outro: Inside the cedar box sits a heavy door key and a floor plan pointing straight behind the hallway bookcase. Don't worry if a word or two went past quickly; they return right away. See you next time.

scenes.title: Move the Books
scenes.summary: F2 joins F1 and M1 in the back hallway to unload the heavy wooden bookcase and uncover a narrow painted door.
scenes.intro: In the quiet back hallway behind the kitchen, {F1} and {M1} stand before a tall wooden bookcase packed with old travel guides. {F2} hurries out of the café corner wiping flour from her hands. Let's listen in first.
story: Is it true? Is there really a secret room behind my kitchen wall?
Help me stack these big green books on the chair, {F2}.
Take the top shelf first so the wood becomes light.
These travel books are older than both of us, {F1}!
That is the last shelf. Ready to pull on three, {M1}?
One, two, three—slide the left side toward me!
Look behind the wood! White paint and a brass keyhole!
A real door, hidden right here in the hallway!
Let us try the big key from the cedar box.
One firm turn to the right... and the latch is open!
Lift the handle first—just like the front door!
scenes.outro: The heavy bookcase is aside and the hidden lock turns cleanly on the first try. Notice how naturally those action words—lift, pull, turn, open—fit together. See you next time.

scenes.title: Glass and Dust
scenes.summary: F1, F2, and M2 step into Room 9—a forgotten glass garden sunroom overlooking the side of the courtyard.
scenes.intro: {F1} pushes the narrow white door open, and morning light filters through dusty glass panes into a quiet forgotten room. {F2} and {M2} step inside behind her in amazement. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: Look at these tall glass windows facing the courtyard tree!
The shutters are closed outside, that is why nobody noticed from the stones!
Now I remember! My uncle called this the winter tea room when I was ten!
Why did someone lock a beautiful bright room behind a bookcase?
The glass roof leaked one rainy spring, and nobody had money to fix it.
Look at the dry stone floor, {M2}—not one drop of water anywhere!
Whoever fixed the courtyard roof years ago fixed this ceiling too!
{M2}, do you see how many small café tables can fit in here?
Wait—to keep our city heritage protection, we promised a public reading café!
And here is the exact room the city letter asked for!
Warm bread, hot tea, morning sun, and zero cold wind!
Wait, what is standing in the corner under that big white cloth?
scenes.outro: Room 9 is a dry, sunlit glass tea room—and something tall is waiting under a white sheet in the corner. Let's find out what it is next time.

scenes.title: Under the White Sheet
scenes.summary: Guest and retired piano teacher F3 helps F1 and M1 pull back the white cloth, revealing an old wooden upright piano.
scenes.intro: Hearing excited voices down the hall, Room 4 guest {F3} walks over with her morning teacup just as {F1} and {M1} reach the tall shape under the white cloth. Listen first.
story: Good morning! Why is everyone standing inside the hallway wall?
Come look, {F3}! We found Room Nine!
Goodness, look at those arched windows! May I step inside?
Watch the dusty threshold, madam. Help me fold this white sheet.
One, two... oh! Look at the dark polished wood!
An upright piano! A real walnut upright piano!
Careful with the lid—it has been closed for decades.
Look at the ivory keys, {F1}. They are clean and whole.
Go ahead, {F3}—play a chord for the house!
Listen... a little low, very warm, and wait—middle D makes no sound!
Every key sings except one stubborn note in the middle?
Give an old piano one good repair, {M1}, and it remembers every song.
scenes.outro: Beneath the dust sheet stands a warm walnut piano with eighty-seven working keys and one silent middle note. See you in the next scene.

scenes.title: Measuring the Sunroom
scenes.summary: Acoustic architect M3 and his older brother M4 inspect the sunroom walls with F1 and confirm the room has wonderful natural sound.
scenes.intro: Ten minutes later, {M3} hurries downstairs with his leather notebook alongside his older brother {M4}, who walked over early from his flat in {CITY} after their Friday reunion. {F1} meets them at the sunroom door. Listen first.
story: {F1}, {F2} told us you unlocked a hidden ninth room!
My little brother grabbed his tape measure before finishing his toast.
Step inside, both of you! Tell us if this room is safe to open.
Four metres wide, six metres long, brick wall on the left, wood ceiling above.
Hear how quiet the street sounds when you clap your hands once?
Zero echo! Wood above glass makes soft music and quiet conversation shine.
So {F2}'s neighbourhood café and {F3}'s piano will not wake the upstairs guests?
Not at all—the thick brick wall blocks every sound from the stairs.
I have the whole weekend free from City Hall, {F1}. Put us both to work!
Can you two help carry the cellar tables in after lunch?
Gladly—working beside {M3} beats sitting at an office desk any day.
First let me sketch the window latches so fresh air flows from the courtyard.
scenes.outro: {M3} approves the acoustics, and {M4} volunteers a pair of strong hands for the weekend. See you next time.

scenes.title: Postcards from May
scenes.summary: Over mid-morning tea, F2, F3, and M1 read the old postcards from the cedar box and learn Room 9 once hosted Friday tea concerts.
scenes.intro: Back at the four-table café corner while {F1} answers the front-desk phone, {F2} pours fresh tea for {F3} and {M1} as they spread the old postcards from the cedar chest across the table. Let's listen in first.
story: Look at this black-and-white photo of our courtyard tree—it only reached the first floor!
Read the back of that blue postcard, madam.
'May tenth, thirty years ago: Tea and piano in Room Nine every Friday at six.'
Every Friday at six! People from the whole street came here for tea and music!
Look at the next card: 'Please save two corner chairs for the baker and the teacher.'
How lovely—this house was already bringing neighbours together thirty years ago.
And next Friday is the first Friday of the month!
Wait—you want to reopen Room Nine next Friday at six o'clock?
Six days to wash the glass, paint the shutters, and bake lemon tarts!
If you can wake up that silent middle key, {M1}, I will gladly play at six.
Fair deal—let us go tell {F1} and {M2} our Friday plan!
Bring the postcard—once {M2} sees this photo, he will say yes!
scenes.outro: Thirty years ago Room 9 welcomed the street every Friday at six, and now {F2}, {F3}, and {M1} are ready to bring the tradition back. See you next time.

scenes.title: Count the Coins
scenes.summary: M2 worries about the cost of renovating Room 9 until F1 and F2 show him a simple low-cost budget.
scenes.intro: At the front desk, {M2} is adding numbers on a notepad with a worried frown when {F1} and {F2} show him the thirty-year-old courtyard postcard. Listen first.
story: I love this old photo, truly, but new café furniture costs a fortune!
Who said anything about buying expensive new furniture, {M2}?
We already have four wooden tables in the cellar and white linen cloths upstairs.
What about chairs, teacups, green shutter paint, and warm wall lamps?
Look at my list: two cans of green paint, twelve simple cups, and market lemons.
And {M3} and {M4} offered to help sand and carry the tables for free!
Wait... let me check your numbers again. Only this much for the whole room?!
Every guesthouse room is full this week, {M2}. We can pay in cash today.
And the city heritage office wants to see our public café open before month's end!
Say yes, {M2}, before you lose your glasses again!
All right—yes! Room Nine opens next Friday at six!
Wonderful! Let us go test the ceiling lamp in the sunroom!
scenes.outro: With a practical budget and full guest rooms upstairs, {M2} gives the green light for Friday at six. One last scene for Episode 1—let's listen.

scenes.title: Don't Touch That Switch
scenes.summary: M2 eagerly flips the old brass wall switch in Room 9 before M1 can check the wires, blowing the ground-floor fuse.
scenes.intro: Back at the threshold of Room 9, {M1} opens his leather tool bag to inspect the old brass wall switch, but an excited {M2} reaches past him beside {F1}. Listen first.
story: Wait one minute before touching that brass switch, {M2}.
Why wait? I remember this glass ceiling lamp—watch how prettily it glows!
Just one quick click—pop! ... Oh dear.
What was that loud pop in the hallway?!
That was the old wire blowing the main ground-floor fuse.
The lobby lamp went dark! Did I break the kitchen oven too?!
Uh-oh—I can hear {F2} calling from the dark kitchen right now!
Thirty-year-old cloth wire, boss. Never flip a switch before I look inside.
Can you fix it before lunch, {M1}? Please say you have spare fuses!
I can reset the kitchen in two minutes, but Room Nine needs new copper wire.
Hold the flashlight steady, {M2}—our six-day countdown just got real!
scenes.outro: One impatient click from {M2} pops the ground-floor fuse and proves Room 9 needs fresh wiring before Friday! Episode 1 of Season 2 is complete—see you in Episode 2.
